title: FATE: Boosting the Performance of Hyper-Dimensional Computing Intelligence with Flexible Numerical DAta TypE
problem: Hyperdimensional Computing (HDC) requires high-precision representations for cosine similarity calculations, making multiplication-heavy computation expensive on resource-constrained edge FPGAs. Binary HDC reduces cost but degrades accuracy significantly.
motivation: HDC is attractive for edge ML due to its light-weight, parallel nature and robustness, but the tension between precision (for accuracy) and low bitwidth (for efficiency) has not been resolved—existing approaches apply uniform quantization across all dimensions.
method: FATE introduces a per-dimension mixed numerical data type scheme for HDC, applying different quantization bitwidths to different dimensions of the hypervector based on their importance. This is combined with sparsity to further reduce computation. The co-design targets embedded FPGA deployment and leverages the observation that not all HDC dimensions contribute equally, enabling high-accuracy inference at lower average precision than uniform quantization.
key_novelty: FATE applies different numerical data types to different dimensions of HDC hypervectors, breaking from the uniform-quantization paradigm to jointly exploit dimension-level importance heterogeneity and sparsity for FPGA acceleration.
contributions: Per-dimension flexible numerical data type assignment for HDC, replacing uniform quantization
Integration of sparsity with mixed-precision quantization to reduce FPGA computational cost
Demonstrated accuracy-efficiency balance on embedded FPGA for HDC workloads

metrics.accuracy: Maintains competitive accuracy vs. full-precision HDC while reducing compute cost vs. binary HDC

limitations: Evaluation is limited to embedded FPGA; generalization to other hardware (ASIC, GPU) not demonstrated.
primary_theme: Per-dimension mixed-precision quantization for hyperdimensional computing on edge FPGA
